cases.input: hi everyone um quick status on project larkspur which is uh the move from the old postgres eleven cluster to the new managed setup on postgres sixteen so where we are we finished the schema freeze on monday the fourteenth no sorry tuesday the fifteenth and since then we've replicated about eighty two percent of the invoices table which is the big one it's roughly four point two terabytes um the logical replication lag has been sitting around ninety seconds during peak which is fine honestly but it spiked to like eleven minutes on thursday night when the nightly reconciliation job kicked off new paragraph the main blocker right now is the ledger underscore entries table it has a column called amt underscore cents that's stored as a numeric with no precision and the new cluster is rejecting about uh three thousand four hundred rows where the value has more than two decimal places which shouldn't even be possible for cents so like something upstream has been writing garbage for a while tomasz thinks it's the refund service from back in twenty twenty one i think he's probably right but we need to confirm before we just round them because rounding money silently is how you end up in an audit new paragraph so the plan is um one tomasz pulls the bad rows into a quarantine table by wednesday two finance signs off on how to fix each one and three we rerun the backfill for that table only we're not going to restart the whole thing new paragraph the cutover date is still pencilled in for saturday march the eighth at two a m wait no we moved it it's march the fifteenth at two a m because of the quarter end freeze the rollback plan is in the runbook at docs slash migrations slash larkspur dash rollback dot md please actually read it before the dry run on the twelfth i know nobody reads runbooks but this one matters um if you're on call that weekend it's dimitri and ana-lucia and i'll be on as backup new paragraph last thing the old cluster costs us about eighteen thousand five hundred dollars a month so every week we slip is real money not just like a vibe so let's get the ledger thing sorted thanks everyone rhea

cases.input: okay so subject line weekly update for haldane brook farm week of march the third um hi everyone so a quick ish update on where we are uh first the herd we had doctor oyelaran out on tuesday no sorry wednesday to check on the three heifers that were limping and it turns out it's not foot rot it's uh just bruising from the new concrete in the collecting yard so she's recommending we put down rubber matting before the end of the month she quoted us roughly two thousand four hundred pounds for the whole yard which is you know more than i wanted but cheaper than losing a cow um milk yields are holding at about twenty six litres per cow per day which is up from twenty four point five last month so that's good news and the tank collection from merriwell dairies is still every second day at six a m so please please make sure the tank room is unlocked by five forty five callum that's mostly aimed at you mate second thing the tractor the old massey is back from pritchard's garage they replaced the hydraulic pump and the bill came to eight hundred and twelve pounds fifty uh which i've paid already so don't worry about that invoice if it lands in the farm inbox third the planting schedule we're going to drill the spring barley on the north field starting on the eighteenth actually let's say the nineteenth because the forecast for the eighteenth is like forty millimetres of rain and i don't want the drill getting stuck again like last year priya can you double check we've got enough seed i think we ordered three point two tonnes but i want to be sure before ewan books the contractor um also the lower paddock fence is still down by the stream so keep the sheep out of there until it's fixed i've asked ewan to get to it by friday last thing uh the open farm day is on saturday the twelfth of april and we've had about sixty families sign up so far which is honestly way more than we expected so i'll need at least four volunteers for the car park and two for the petting pen just reply to this email if you can help okay i think that's everything uh thanks all for a really solid week cheers martha

bella she's the golden retriever in kennel four uh she came in at about two thirty with suspected bloat we did the x-rays and it's not a full twist thank god so we decompressed her and she's on fluids at sixty mils an hour no sorry eighty mils an hour I bumped it up around six she needs her next dose of maropitant at ten pm and then you know just keep an eye on her abdomen if it starts getting
